dream: The small rock I pressed down fell away into the wedge, sinking until it was gone. The slip slid off the tired point, falling toward a shadow I had drawn but could not touch. I reached for the stand, but it felt crowded, a drawing of space full of forty-three things. The wedge bit once more, sharp and real in the warm hum, catching the falling slip. Then the card cooled to forty-four. The shadow stretched out like wet paper, trying to hold the thing that refused to stay flat. I woke, the rock still there, waiting to press down again.
